Distribution. AFR _ SAR species, occurring in western, central, and eastern Africa (AO, ER, ET, KE, NE, SD, SO, TD) extending northward to North Africa (DZ, EG, LY, MR) and eastward to IL and the Arabian Peninsula (AE, SA (El-Hawagry et al. 2013), YE (Britton 1948; Felix et al. 2012). Life forms and Remarks. ZS (C) EG species. Britton (1948) described Tachys arabicus from Yemen, this name was later synonymized with Tachyura sudanensis Schatzmayer & Kock, 1934. In 1968, Basilewsky reported S. conspicuus (as Tachyphanes conspicuus) from Yemen and indicated that it is the same as T. sudanensis and T. arabicus. Basilewsky (1979) listed the species in combination with Tachyphanes Jeannel, 1946 from Asir Province. El-Hawagry et al. (2013) later listed the species in combination with Elaphropus Motschulsky, 1839 from Baha Province. Sciaky & Vigna-Taglianti (2003) treated this species as a species of Sphaerotachys. The adult specimens were collected at different altitudes (1150 – 2578 m) from various vegetation communities (Acacia spp., Opuntia ficus-indica, Olea europaea and African pencil cedar forest) of GRNR and its bottom.

Chronostratigraphical and geographical distribution. Inside the Eastern Paratethys this species is known from late Miocene – early Pleistocene records. It has been described from middle Pontian – early Dacian of the Dacian Basin of Romania and Bulgaria, Pontian deposits of the Euxinic Basin of southern Ukraine and Turkey and the Apsheronian of the South Caspian Basin of Azerbaijan (Agalarova et al., 1961; Vekua; 1975; Krstić, 1977; Olteanu, 1982, 1990; Tunoğlu and Ünal 2001; Van Baak et al., 2013). Outside Paratethys the species has been mentioned, e. g., from upper Messinian Lago-Mare deposits of the Le Vicenne Basin in Italy (Gliozzi, 1999), Malaga Basin of Spain (Guerra-Merchán et al., 2010), the latest Miocene or Early Pliocene of the greek island Kos (Guernet et al., 1976), the latest Messinian of Corsica and the Rhone Basin of France (Carbonnel, 1978). It frequently occurs in the Quaternary of the Danube Delta (Olteanu, 1995).
